answer.rationale: Memory 73 explicitly warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable—the acquired cohort in exp_73 did not survive first renewal, retention dropped 12%, and this is precisely the trap leadership is tempted into today. Promotional pricing is a short-term bleed that compounds churn. Instead, the durable memory shows three reliable levers: (1) Activation messaging (memory_91) improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to meaningful action—directly addresses why price-sensitive SMBs churn: they haven't yet perceived value. (2) Signup simplification (memory_31) improved SMB activation with retention holding steady, proving engagement-path improvements work on this segment. (3) Referral incentives (memory_57) added qualified revenue in established customers without measurable retention harm—can activate existing base to defend against competitor poaching. A three-pronged activation push (messaging + streamlined onboarding + referral leverage) targets the root cause: perceived low value-to-price ratio. This preserves long-term cohort quality while buying time. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is secondary but should remain in pipeline for high-touch retention of at-risk large accounts. This is not a discounting race; it is a value-perception race.
